direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels like a natural progression for this world, as it has the charm of the first movie; It also feels a bit more mature and less feel-good than the first movie, showing how the comedy world has changed since the 2000s; The direction on a microscale is pretty good, as it just lets these actors play, and it is great seeing them all back together after 20 years; The direction on a microscale also helps show the themes of the movie, as it is very much social commentary on the digital age and how it is impacting journalism and publishing; The storytelling is pretty simple and similar to the first movie

performance.comments: Basically picks up where she left off as she still embodies the terrifying yet iconic fashion legend that is Miranda Priestly (basically Anna Wintour); her chemistry is stronger in the movie as she is given more scenes to actually play with other characters, rather than basically acting on-top of everyone else; her character is bit more humainzed in this movie as she does feel more emphatic towards others, which is nice to see after 20 years but also kinda ruins the appeal for her character

Her performance really shows the growth she's had in her career over the last 20 years as while she still is the queen of the 2000s feel-good movie, she has had more experience playing more complex characters and it shows in her performance; still has great chemistry with the cast, especially Meryl Streep as she is given more scenes to work with her; her dynamic with Tucci starts off not as strong as the original, but by the end of the movie feels like it is a natural progression from the first as the dynamic still is the heart of the movie;Still a baddie cause she's always gonna be a baddie
Kinda takes a step back in this sequel as she is more of a minor character, but she still does have her charm and has good chemistry with Anne Hathaway
He's kinda just there playing the archetype of the Tech Billionare looking to buy out fashion, a la Jeff Bezos
I have no idea how they conviced him to be in this movie because he is too talented to be here, and it shows cause he is so effortless in his role

Has definitely aged since the first movie and it does take some time to warm up to his character again, but by the end of the movie, he is still the heart of the movie as he still has great chemistry with Anne Hathaway, still believing in her potential and very feel do

cast.comments: Typical big budget legacy sequel cast, with the new characters trying to mesh with the old characters

story.comments: The concept is nice to see from a legacy sequel, as it does not repeat the same story as the first; Because the story is very different from the first, it requires you to watch the first movie to understand the context, as there is little exposition given; This movie basically picks up 20 years later and sees how the characters are doing as their lives intersect in somewhat of a reunion, showing how their world is very different this time around with the advent of the digital age; The plot structure feels like a tale of two halves, as the first half sets the scene for the second; The first half transitions from a reunion special in New York to an action-packed Milan fashion week; The character writing is not as strong as the first, as it is less symbolic, but it does show the growth or stagnation in some of these characters and still keeps the core of Tucci and Hathaway's relationship

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty good and has evolved with the times, even making fun of how the world has changed since the 2000s; The humor is good, as many of the jokes are about how the world has changed since we last saw these characters, and it feels like everyone is able to play off each other because of their history together; The symbolism is different this time around, as much of the messaging with this movie is about critiquing the digital age and how it has changed journalism and publishing, making the movie feel more like social commentary and less timeless than the first movie; The change from feel-good to more grounded storytelling symbolizes how comedies have changed since the 2000s, and the dichotomy between these two movies shows that; The opening scene with the two belts shows how it took 20 years for the item discussed in the first movie to now be vended on the street; The ending scene with Anne Hathaway wearing her blue sweater mirrors the first movie, showing how confident she is in herself and her style, maturing from the insecure new-grad she was in the first movie; The foreshadowing is pretty good, as it makes the movie feel bookended

score.comments: Uses many of the same themes as the first, which helps with the nostalgia and adds to the tone

soundtrack.comments: Helps make this movie feel like it's for the girls during this era

cinematography.comments: Definitely the worst part of the movie, as it tries to do way too much with its pans and handheld shots, so it just looks messy and tacky for a big-budget film

editing.comments: Definitely does not feel as cool as the first movie, as it only has one dress montage shot, which is not as good as the first and only feels like it is there for fan service; It is used poorly in conjunction with the cinematography when it tries to do too much, but it is fine for most of the movie

sound.comments: Definitely not as bad as the first movie, as the music does not drown out the dialogue

production_design.comments: Shows the evolution of Runway and the fashion world over the last 20 years, featuring renovated sets in New York and the high fashion and history of Milan

makeup.comments: Helps paint these characters as fashion icons and makes the characters look like they are following the trends of the current time

costumes.comments: Still the best part of the movie, as it continues to highlight the fashion world and the characters' personalities through their clothing, with Andi's wardrobe definitely feeling influenced by her time at Runway in the first movie; There is symbolism in the costumes as well, as the fine combination Anne Hathaway wears mimics the outfit Meryl Streep critiques in the first movie, but this time Andi feels more confident in her outfit

review.pacing: Pacing is not as strong this time around, as this movie feels like two halves, and because of this, the movie can feel too slow or too fast at different times
review.climax: The climax is what you would expect from a legacy sequel comedy, but it does provide closure for all the arcs in this movie, making another sequel feel irrelevant
review.tone: The tone very much shows the evolution of comedy since the 2000s, as it is less feel-good and more grounded while trying to provide social commentary, but it still has some of the charm of the first movie
review.overall: Overall, 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' is surprisingly a pretty good legacy sequel that shows the evolution of comedy since the 2000s, as it is less feel-good and more grounded with social commentary on the digital age influencing journalism and publishing, but it still has some of the charm of the first movie; It is great to see these characters again, especially Anne Hathaway and Stanley Tucci's dynamic, as they all fall back into place and make this movie feel like a natural progression from the original, but it does have its flaws like its cinematography and pacing that hold it back from being as good as the first movie
